claims.text: Pre-coating W particles with Ti before SPS will cause an interfacial Ti–Cu compound to form in situ.
The interfacial Ti–Cu compound will improve wetting between W and Cu.
Improved W–Cu interfacial bonding will minimize phase separation and void formation.
The Ti-coated material will have superior thermal transport under irradiation.
The Ti-coated material will preserve mechanical durability under irradiation.
Conventionally processed W–Cu structures suffer from inhomogeneous interfaces, void formation, and phase separation.
A thin Ti coating can be deposited on W particles by vapor deposition before SPS consolidation with Cu.
SPS can be performed below the melting point of W and the boiling point of Cu in a controlled atmosphere.
The in-situ Ti–Cu intermetallic layer will act as a diffusion barrier at W/Cu interfaces.
During SPS, deposited Ti will react with Cu at W surfaces to form a transient intermetallic compound.
The transient intermetallic compound will increase effective wetting and bonding at W/Cu interfaces.
Improved interfacial wetting and bonding will reduce void formation and phase separation while maintaining mechanical cohesion under irradiation.
SPS of Ti-coated W–Cu powders will yield a denser and more microstructurally uniform composite.
The Ti-coated W–Cu composite will have fewer voids and better thermal transport under irradiation than uncoated conventional W–Cu composites.
Mechanical durability of the Ti-coated composite will match or exceed that of conventional W–Cu composites.

Direct infiltration, uncoated powder sintering, and mechanical alloying followed by SPS typically produce W–Cu composites with interfacial imperfections, phase separation, and voids that impair thermal transport.
The intervention is applicable to fusion-reactor joint materials fabricated by SPS.
Applicability is limited by the ability to deposit uniform Ti coatings and by the long-term irradiation stability of the Ti–Cu interlayer.
The magnitude of thermal-conductivity and mechanical-strength improvements under realistic fusion irradiation is uncertain.
The identity and thickness of the intermetallic layer may vary with SPS parameters.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome allows mechanical durability merely to match the baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires enhanced mechanical durability. An equal-durability result could therefore satisfy the prediction but still trigger falsification.
